clue.text: Conservative girl in charge is member in Greek style

parts.note: a lass is a girl
M is an abbreviation for member, as in MP

explanation.surface: A Tory woman who runs things sits as an elected member and favours a Hellenic look.
explanation.definitionFit: Classicism is the artistic principle of following ancient Greek and Roman models, hence a Greek style.

clue.text: Reported free by Leonard, and thus offering rum and cola

definitions.text: Reported free by Leonard, and thus offering rum and cola

parts.words: Reported free by Leonard, and thus offering rum and cola
parts.note: Elmore Leonard's novel ... Libre names an island said to be free, and a ... Libre is also the cocktail of rum and cola

explanation.surface: A writer's report of liberty turns into an offer of a mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Libre is Spanish for free, so the island 'reported free' in Elmore Leonard's title is the one whose name also begins the drink Cuba Libre, rum with cola and lime.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean island gives its name both to Leonard's novel title and to the rum-and-cola cocktail.

clue.text: His expertise is Eng Lit (may also be lasting)

indicators.note: the letters of the word may also be arranged as something else, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A scholar of English literature whose interest is said to be enduring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may also be' tells you the letters of LASTING can be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglist is a specialist in English language and literature, a scholar of the subject.

clue.text: Dickens lawyer sounds like powerful chap, having money

indicators.note: the strongman's name is spoken and a near-identical spelling with a P is entered

parts.note: Samson is the biblical strongman
brass is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A lawyer from a Victorian novel sounds like a strongman with plenty of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Sampson Brass is the crooked attorney in Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop; the biblical Samson is said aloud and spelt with a P. Brass is northern British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Sampson Brass is the shady attorney in The Old Curiosity Shop, a lawyer created by Dickens.

clue.text: Provenance of Brecht's circle

parts.note: Brecht's play The Caucasian Chalk Circle names the region its circle comes from

explanation.definitionFit: Brecht's play title calls its chalk circle Caucasian, so the mountain region is where it originates.

clue.text: American language, partly nasal, is hard to imitate

indicators.note: only part of the words nasal, is hard is used, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: A tongue spoken by Native Americans, rather nasal, is tricky to copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' marks the run naSAL IS Hard; 'to imitate' completes the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Salish is a family of Native American languages spoken in the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Remain intense, say, like Oscar

explanation.surface: Staying fiercely engaged in the manner of a famous wit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remain intense, say' is heard as 'remain in tents', to camp out; Oscar Wilde's affected flamboyance is the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To camp is to stay in tents, and camp also means theatrically flamboyant, the manner of Oscar Wilde.

clue.text: "… a spirit still, and bright/ With something of — light" (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: "… a spirit still, and bright/ With something of — light" (Wordsworth)

parts.words: "… a spirit still, and bright/ With something of — light" (Wordsworth)
parts.note: the missing word completes a line of Wordsworth's poem She Was a Phantom of Delight, an adjective for heavenly radiance

explanation.surface: A line of Wordsworth's verse with one word left blank for the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation comes from Wordsworth's She Was a Phantom of Delight; the gap holds the adjective for an angel's light.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem describes the woman's radiance as heavenly, like that of a celestial being from heaven.

clue.text: Iron strength of spirit required before printing?

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them
proof is the measure of alcoholic strength in spirits

explanation.surface: A firm resolve is needed before a printing job goes ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strength of spirit' looks like courage, but it means the alcohol content of a spirit, its proof.
explanation.definitionFit: A press proof is the trial impression checked and approved before a print run goes ahead.

clue.text: How Rochester would have at first married Jane

definitions.text: How Rochester would have at first married Jane

parts.words: How Rochester would have at first married Jane
parts.note: in Jane Eyre, Rochester's first wedding to Jane is halted because he already has a living wife, Bertha

explanation.surface: Asks about the manner of a famous fictional first wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The wedding in Jane Eyre is stopped because Rochester's first wife is alive in the attic; going ahead would have meant two spouses at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying while already wed is bigamy, which Rochester would have committed with a second spouse.

clue.text: American novelist seen to mature and come to the point

parts.note: to age is to mature
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A US writer is seen to grow older and finally get to the heart of things.
explanation.walkthrough: James Agee wrote A Death in the Family. 'the point' is a compass point, E.
explanation.definitionFit: James Agee was a writer from Tennessee, author of A Death in the Family.

clue.text: German musician who led children astray

definitions.text: German musician who led children astray

parts.words: German musician who led children astray
parts.note: the legendary piper of Hamelin, in Lower Saxony, lured the town's children away with his music

explanation.definitionFit: In the legend of Hamelin the colourfully dressed piper lures the town's children away after being cheated of his fee.

clue.text: One of a 2X collection by-Roald Dahl

definitions.text: One of a 2X collection by-Roald Dahl

parts.words: One of a 2X collection by-Roald Dahl
parts.note: X stands for a ..., so 2X is a doubled ..., the title of Roald Dahl's short-story collection

explanation.surface: A single item from a book of stories with an odd numbered title.
explanation.walkthrough: X is the written sign for a kiss, so 2X spells the title of Dahl's 1960 collection Kiss Kiss; one of the pair is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahl's story collection is titled with the word for a peck on the lips said twice, so one is a single smooch.

clue.text: Marathon participant outlasted many in dramatic competition

definitions.text: Marathon participant outlasted many in dramatic competition

parts.words: Marathon participant outlasted many in dramatic competition
parts.note: the Greek tragedian fought at the battle of Marathon and won many prizes at the Athenian drama festivals

explanation.surface: A long-distance runner kept going longer than most in a theatrical contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Marathon is the battle of 490 BC, not the race; the Athenian tragedian fought there and later won the Dionysia drama contest many times.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian tragedian fought the Persians at Marathon and took first prize at the Dionysia repeatedly.

clue.text: Celebrity king snake at bleak farm

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
an adder is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A famous monarch meets a viper on a cheerless farm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Starkadders are the grim family at Cold Comfort Farm in Stella Gibbons's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Starkadder is the family name of the gloomy clan living at Cold Comfort Farm in Stella Gibbons's comic novel.

clue.text: Roman playwright, with a name for comedies, changes it in suit, perhaps

definitions.text: Roman playwright, with a name for comedies

indicators.note: the letters of it in suit are changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient comic dramatist alters a costume, perhaps for the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges IT IN SUIT. Titinius wrote Roman comedies in native dress, the fabula togata; 'perhaps' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Titinius was an early Roman writer known for comedies set in Italian everyday life.

clue.text: It provides room for new recaps

indicators.note: new tells you the letters of recaps are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Something gives space so that summaries can be rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges RECAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacer is a device or piece inserted to keep a gap between parts.

clue.text: She was finally trained by Tolstoy

definitions.text: She was finally trained by Tolstoy

parts.words: She was finally trained by Tolstoy
parts.note: Tolstoy's heroine ends her life under a train, so at the end she is 'trained'

explanation.surface: A woman completed her coaching under a Russian master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' means not coached but killed by a train: Tolstoy's heroine throws herself under one at the novel's end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolstoy's adulterous heroine dies beneath a train, the novel's tragic end for her.

clue.text: Afterthoughts suggesting Jilly Cooper characters

explanation.surface: Second thoughts call to mind a popular novelist's people.
explanation.walkthrough: Riders is Jilly Cooper's novel of show-jumping; riders are also clauses added to a document as afterthoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders are clauses appended to a document, and Cooper's show-jumping novel Riders is full of horsemen.

clue.text: Closely follow pop music from David Foster

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
rock is a kind of popular music

explanation.surface: Tail a record producer's pop output closely.
explanation.walkthrough: David Foster is the Australian novelist whose comic Dog Rock (1985) is set in a country town, not the music producer of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog Rock is a 1985 comic novel by Australian writer David Foster.

clue.text: Borrow story from travelling man

parts.note: George Borrow wrote a novel of wandering among the Romany, named after the word master he was called by them

explanation.surface: Take a tale on loan from a wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borrow' is not the verb but George Borrow, whose 1851 book follows a wanderer among the Romany.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavengro, Romany for word master, is George Borrow's semi-autobiographical tale of life on the road.

clue.text: Browning observed that he sat and played toccatas, stately at the clavichord

definitions.text: Browning observed that he sat and played toccatas, stately at the clavichord

parts.words: Browning observed that he sat and played toccatas, stately at the clavichord
parts.note: the words quote Browning's poem A Toccata of — 's, about a Venetian composer

explanation.surface: A poet recalls a musician who played keyboard pieces with dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning's poem is A Toccata of Galuppi's, about the Venetian composer Baldassare Galuppi; the clue paraphrases its line about toccatas at the clavichord.
explanation.definitionFit: Baldassare Galuppi was the Venetian composer whose keyboard toccatas inspire Browning's poem.

clue.text: He is on Naipaul's street

parts.note: Naipaul's first written book names a Port of Spain street after a Spanish man's name

explanation.surface: A man lives in the road a Trinidadian author wrote about.
explanation.walkthrough: V. S. Naipaul's Miguel Street portrays the residents of a street in Port of Spain, Trinidad.
explanation.definitionFit: Naipaul's book is titled after a Spanish man's name used as a Port of Spain street name.

clue.text: Hippo man who left his confessions

definitions.text: Hippo man who left his confessions

parts.words: Hippo man who left his confessions
parts.note: Hippo is the North African city whose bishop wrote the Confessions

explanation.surface: Someone associated with a river beast who wrote down his admissions.
explanation.walkthrough: Hippo is not the animal but Hippo Regius in North Africa, whose bishop wrote the Confessions.
explanation.definitionFit: The saint was Bishop of Hippo and author of the autobiographical Confessions.

clue.text: Limit of Nabokov's fire

explanation.surface: The boundary of a Russian-American writer's blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: A pale is a boundary, as in 'beyond the pale'; Nabokov's novel is Pale Fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale is a fence or boundary, and Nabokov's novel title couples the word with fire.

clue.text: Waugh's men were at it

parts.note: Evelyn Waugh's novel title says where his men were, the first book of the Sword of Honour trilogy

explanation.surface: A writer's soldiers were busy doing something.
explanation.walkthrough: Men at Arms (1952) is the first novel of Evelyn Waugh's Sword of Honour trilogy.
explanation.definitionFit: Waugh's novel is Men at Arms, so his men were at weapons, in military service.

clue.text: Tomlinson's was in the wall

parts.note: the title refers to a story of an opening in a wall, a well-known literary image

explanation.surface: Someone's possession was set into the masonry.
explanation.walkthrough: The image is 'the door in the wall', the title of a famous H. G. Wells story, here credited to Tomlinson.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance set into a wall is a doorway, the opening in the story's title.

clue.text: Il Prete Rosso left some notes on it

definitions.text: Il Prete Rosso left some notes on it

parts.words: Il Prete Rosso left some notes on it
parts.note: the Red Priest was Vivaldi's nickname, and a composer writes his notes on staved sheets

explanation.surface: An Italian cleric jotted down a few remarks somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Il Prete Rosso, the Red Priest, was Vivaldi's nickname; his 'notes' are musical ones, written on staved sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled sheets with staves are where a composer like Vivaldi writes down musical notation.

clue.text: Artist returning British pottery in Japanese style

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for an artist

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for Britain is read backwards

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, stands for British

explanation.surface: A painter comes home with Japanese-style ceramics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns UK into KU, after RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Raku is a hand-shaped, low-fired Japanese earthenware used in the tea ceremony.

clue.text: Reportedly change waders in chancel

indicators.note: the word for change is heard and written as a near-identical church word

parts.note: to alter is to change
rails are wading marsh birds

explanation.surface: Word has it that wading birds are being modified inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Waders are birds here, the rails of marshland, not fishermen's boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Altar-rails are the low barrier in a church chancel where communicants kneel.
